status: partial: CPU stage measured; GPU parity (f5) and 1080p cost (f6) not run
machine: the author's Windows 11 workstation. CPU results: g++ 13.2 (MinGW-w64, Release) for the orbit and scale runs and the GCC-family tests; MSVC (VS 2026, Release) for the second test run.

f1_temporal.config: pre-registered: px 2, cell 0.1, 48 frames at 320 x 180, frames 1 to 47, 10,000 paired bootstrap resamples, seed 20261022

ink.verdict: HOLDS (by 0.027; prediction 0.6 to 0.85 was too high)

f1_temporal.note: the intervals are narrow because they resample 47 correlated frames of one orbit of one scene; they do not cover other scenes or paths.

f2_controls.verdict: screen and shuffled-anchor controls fail the 0.50 bound as required. The scale-term-broken control fails f1 (0.415 on ink) and fails f3 (below).

control_scale_term_broken.verdict: fails as required (prediction was 'well above 3'; 2.96 is a small miss of the stated size)

runs.f4_structure: tests/test_fractal_dither.cpp: rank_K at K = 3 equals bayer8Rank; blend equals coarse at m = 0 and fine at m = 1; marginal uniform within 3% at m = 0.25, 0.5, 0.75; every coarse-lit cell keeps its corner sub-cell lit. HOLDS on GCC and on MSVC.
runs.f7_goldens: level-plane FNV-1a of orbit frame 0 at 256 x 144 pinned in tests/test_fractal_dither.cpp (fractal ink 5ac361b7dfe0a6bb, fractal tones4 922c22c7c711d410, screen ink 31c2b5c49d02867d). HOLDS: the same hashes on GCC and MSVC.
runs.f5_gpu_parity: NOT RUN. The WGSL branch (style.wgsl, HLSL regenerated, wgsl_to_hlsl --check clean) and the runner (src/renderer/gpu/fractal_gpu.cpp, raw_native_cli fractal-dither gpu) are written and compile in the D3D12 build. No device ran them. No WARP, lavapipe or RTX 4090 result exists.
runs.f6_cost: NOT RUN. The timestamp harness (DitherTiming in style_gpu.cpp, fractal-dither gpu --cost) compiles; nothing was timed.

f8_accuracy.reading: recorded, not gated. The 2026-10-15 trade-off reappears: a surface-attached pattern gives up tone accuracy. Fractal costs about 4x the screen anchor's error on ink and about 40% less error than the world-octave snap.

stability_against_accuracy.reading: On this orbit the existing world-octave anchor is more stable than the fractal anchor on both presets and has the larger tone error. The fractal anchor's gain over world-octave is lower error and no octave seam, not lower instability. This work does not show the fractal anchor beats world-octave on the instability metric; it shows the reverse.

exploratory.what: px sweep at 1, 1.5 and 3, run after seeing the px 2 result, files evidence/fractal-dither/orbit-px*-exploratory.json. They decide nothing and the pre-registered px 2 is not changed.
exploratory.reading: reduction rises with cell size and so does tone error. At px 3 tones4 would pass the bound at A = 3.14 against the screen anchor's 0.67.

images: evidence/fractal-dither/images (frames 0 and 24; screen, world-octave, fractal), looked at: the fractal frame shows banded moire on the oblique ground, where the depth-only scale term ignores foreshortening. The scene's tones sit near mid grey, the hardest case for flip rate.
overall: f1 holds for ink and misses for tones4, so the bound as written (both presets) is NOT met. Kill criterion not hit. f2, f3, f4, f7 hold. f5 and f6 are not run.
does_not_prove: Anything about the GPU pass, its parity or its cost. Perception. Other scenes, grazing angles, moving objects. That fractal beats world-octave.
